title: Encoding, framing and error control
subtitle: Turning bits into voltages, marking where frames start and end, and noticing — or fixing — the bit that got flipped.

encoding.title: Line coding
encoding.body: A wire carries voltages, so bits must be mapped to levels. NRZ-L holds a level for the whole bit; NRZ-I flips level for a 1. Both lose the clock on long runs of identical bits. Manchester puts a transition in the middle of every bit (low→high for 1, high→low for 0), so the receiver recovers the clock at the cost of double the signal rate — the code of classic 10 Mb/s Ethernet. Bipolar AMI sends 0 as no pulse and alternates + and − for 1s.

framing.title: Framing and byte stuffing
framing.body: The data link layer must tell the receiver where a frame starts and ends. A flag byte (HDLC uses 01111110) does it; to stop data that happens to contain the flag confusing the receiver, the sender inserts extra bits — bit stuffing: after five consecutive 1s in the data, insert a 0, which the receiver removes.
framing.steps: Data: 0111111011 (contains six 1s in a row). After the first five 1s insert a 0 so the flag pattern 01111110 cannot appear inside the data.

crc.title: Error detection: parity, checksum, CRC
crc.body: A single parity bit catches any odd number of flipped bits but no even number. The checksum adds the words and sends the complement. The CRC treats the message as a polynomial and sends the remainder of dividing by an agreed generator G(x): the receiver divides the whole frame and accepts only a zero remainder. It catches all single-bit errors, all bursts up to the generator’s degree, and almost everything else. Dividing 1101011011 by 10011 gives the CRC 1110; the frame sent is 11010110111110.

hamming.title: Error correction: Hamming code
hamming.body: Detection needs a retransmission; Hamming codes let the receiver correct a single-bit error itself. Parity bits sit at positions 1, 2, 4, 8…; parity bit p covers every position whose binary index contains p. After an error the failing parity checks, read as a binary number, give the position of the bad bit — the syndrome. Data 1011 encodes to 0110011; corrupt bit 5 and the syndrome reads 5.
hamming.steps: 4 data bits need r parity bits with 2ʳ ≥ 4 + r + 1. So Hamming(7,4): 7 bits sent for 4 data bits.

protocols.title: PPP, HDLC and Ethernet
protocols.body: HDLC and PPP frame point-to-point links with flags, an address/control field, a payload and a CRC. Ethernet (IEEE 802.3) frames carry destination and source MAC (6 bytes each), a type, 46–1500 bytes of data and a 4-byte CRC. The data link layer is split into LLC (flow and error control, protocol multiplexing) and MAC (who may transmit, and addressing).

summary.title: Summary
summary.body:
• Line coding maps bits to signals; Manchester embeds the clock.
  • Framing needs flags and bit stuffing.
  • CRC detects, Hamming corrects single errors.
